title: Make hostname resolution for loopback address more robust.

timeline.message:
Make hostname resolution for loopback address more robust.

Implemented a fall-back to `localhost` when FQDN for
loopback address (`127.0.0.1`) cannot be resolved.
This can happen if test platform's DNS resolution
is not properly configured.
timeline.author: Slobodan Adamovic

timeline.body:
Implemented a fall-back to `localhost` when FQDN for
loopback address (`127.0.0.1`) cannot be resolved.
This can happen if test platform's DNS resolution
is not properly configured.

Closes #89324

Could this instead be due to the security manager not having permissions to delegate ?

It looks like we already added a few aliases here: 
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/qa/kerberos-tests/src/javaRestTest/resources/plugin-security.policy via https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/32588

I wonder if due to implementation order (order defined?) we just pick a different alias and the security manager is preventing the use of the chosen alias. If that is the case, then I think we should change the comments here and maybe look into a different fix ?

related: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.security.jgss/javax/security/auth/kerberos/DelegationPermission.html

reply.body:
> Could this instead be due to the security manager not having permissions to delegate ?

I've checked it and it's not caused by the security manager. I've also [reproduced it](https://gist.github.com/slobodanadamovic/57057bf1741e86a95ee560475dfad2e3) with a custom `hosts` file by passing it as `-Djdk.net.hosts.file`.

> do we even test non-loopback address?

We don't. We resolve only `127.0.0.1` which is defined in `build.gradle` file:

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/e4ff839e4cab6d443d1b43d10733029ae0afecd3/x-pack/qa/kerberos-tests/build.gradle#L19

and we expect it later to be resolved to `localhost` since we set up `HTTP/localhost` in keytab file:
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/cbda0a51c654b6b0657abd3b46813de712edb34d/test/fixtures/krb5kdc-fixture/src/main/resources/provision/peppa.sh#L6

> So that we use a fixed name to refer to any loopback addresses ?

Initially I took similar approach to return `localhost` without even attempting to resolve `127.0.0.1` address, but then decided to actually try to resolve it and fail if it's not resolved. Reasoning was to make it future proof and fail fast in case the `http.host` gets changed for some reason.
